title: Item:Thieves' Tools
wikitext:
[[File:50 +5 Thieves' Tools.jpg|thumb|right|300px|A set of Thieves' Tools]]
Thieves' Tools are a ''required'' item for the use of [[Open Lock]] and [[Disable Device]] skills. If you have no Tools in your Inventory, you cannot perform either of these tasks.

Thieves' Tools provide a bonus to the skill roll ranging from +1 to +7. Basic Tools provide a +1 bonus, [[Masterwork#Masterwork Thieves' Tools|Masterwork]] Tools provide a +2 bonus, and magically enchanted tools provide an additional bonus from +1 to +5. While Masterwork Tools are clearly labelled, higher-tier tools retain their "+X" naming convention, even though their actual dice roll bonus is higher – for example, +5 Thieves' Tools grant a +7 bonus to Disable Device and Open Lock. 
The maximum stack size is 1,000 in a single [[inventory]] or [[bank]] slot.

=== Sources of Thieves' Tools ===

Thieves' Tools are typically bought and found in stacks of 50. 

They can be acquired in numerous ways:

* Basic Thieves' Tools (+1 bonus) can be purchased from any [[General Vendor]]
* Masterwork Thieves' Tools (+2 bonus) are sold by [[Raef Larksong]] (found in the [[The Marketplace Bazaar]] and the [[Hall of Heroes|Eberron Hall of Heroes]])
** Raef also sells Basic tools like any General Vendor.
* found in chests, with quality dependent on [[Looting#Chest Level|Chest Level]].
* Thieves' Tools with a total skill bonus of +1 to +6 (to Disable Device or Open Lock) can be purchased from the [[The Free Agents|Free Agents]] vendor, [[Sorvile Smythe]] (found in [[The Harbor]] across from the gate to [[The Marketplace]]). You need 75 Favor to buy Basic, Masterwork, +1, or +2 tools (+1 to +4 skill bonus) and 150 Favor for +3 and +4 enchanted tools (+5/+6 skill bonus). Magical "Free Agent" tools (+1 to +4) from Sorvile are [[Bound to Character|Bound to Character on Acquire]] and do not stack with other tools with the same bonus.
* bought from the Auction House (in varying stack sizes, and varying asking prices)
* constructed with Trap Parts (see [[Thieves' Tools#Construction|below]]) [[File:3 Rusty Thieves' Tools.png|thumb|right|300px|A set of Rusty Thieves' Tools]]
:* Note:  "Rusty Thieves' Tools" also exist and can be purchased (base price of 1 gold) from [[Elspeth Wright]] after completing the [[The Lost Seekers]] (Waterworks) story arc. However, their maximum stack size is only 3, (not 1,000<!-- as per U25 -->) in a single inventory slot. Rusty Thieves' Tools provide: Open Lock Bonus: −2 and Disable Device Bonus: −2. Obviously, these should only be purchased as an extreme emergency measure.

== Using Thieves' Tools ==
Thieves' Tools have no minimum level which largely makes the +5 variety obviously preferable. As many traps will injure a character on a failed roll (and some chests are also trapped), any character wishing to use [[Open Lock]] or [[Disable Device]] should use the best tools they can, and may want to consider the acquisition of +5 Tools as a priority.

When you attempt to Open Locks or Disable Devices with Tools, the game automatically deducts 1 Tool from the stack, regardless if the attempt was successful or not.

If you have more than one stack of Tools in your Inventory (possibly with different bonuses), the game will automatically select, add the bonus from, and deduct 1 Tool from ''the first stack listed'' (reading left to right, top to bottom, starting with the first Inventory tab). This means that the game does '''not''' automatically use "the best" Tools in your inventory! It is advised that Trap specialists always keep the stack they prefer to use permanently in the very first slot (top left corner, 1st tab) in their pack, so any lesser quality "found" tools are not accidentally used instead.

In part because of this, the bonus from Thieves' Tools is '''not''' reflected in the Skill Totals listed on the Character Sheet.

* Tip: Some players will drag/drop their stack of Thieves' Tools to a hotbar slot, so they have a constant visual count of the number of tools they have remaining. It is generally considered extremely bad form for a trap disarmer to run out of tools in the middle of a quest.

See the [[DDO information project/Traps and locks|DDO information project]] for DC's of Traps and Locks throughout the game.

== Construction ==
In a [[Device Workstation]] combine a number of Mechanical Trap Parts and a weapon with the corresponding enhancement bonus (the weapon will be consumed in the crafting process) to create a set of 50 Thieves' Tools.

The [[Trapmaking]] Feat is '''not required''' for the manufacture of Thieves' Tools. However, a character without the Trapmaking Feat will need to acquire the Mechanical Trap Parts from another character.

*  10 Mechanical Trap Parts and a +1 weapon for 50 +1 Thieves' Tools
*  25 Mechanical Trap Parts and a +2 weapon for 50 +2 Thieves' Tools
*  50 Mechanical Trap Parts and a +3 weapon for 50 +3 Thieves' Tools
*  75 Mechanical Trap Parts and a +4 weapon for 50 +4 Thieves' Tools
* 100 Mechanical Trap Parts and a +5 weapon for 50 +5 Thieves' Tools

Note: +6 and greater weapons cannot be used to make thieves' tools.
